key_insight: UniD shows that a single video model can learn to predict many dense scene properties at once, even when the training annotations come from different datasets that do not overlap. The key idea is to unify fragmented supervision without relying on expensive pseudo-label generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the problem of training unified scene-understanding models when annotations for depth, normals, semantics, motion, and other dense tasks are scattered across incompatible datasets. Existing approaches either require fully co-annotated data or costly pseudo-labeling, which limits scalability.
method: Train one unified video model (UniD) to jointly predict eight dense scene properties from disjoint training data.
Use a shared representation so knowledge transfers across tasks and video frames, reducing dependence on task-specific fully labeled datasets.
Avoid large-scale pseudo-labeling by directly learning from fragmented annotations across datasets.
impact: This matters because it makes multi-task dense prediction more practical and scalable for real-world AI systems. Practitioners can build stronger unified models from the data they already have, instead of collecting expensive all-in-one annotations.
